findings_remediated.finding: The node teaches operational capacity, bottlenecks and capacity utilisation, but the mapped promotion sources did not directly support those concepts and the utilisation calculation strongly enough.
findings_remediated.remediation: Add direct CC BY evidence for capacity utilisation as actual output relative to maximum output and for a bottleneck as a capacity-constraining resource. Teaching content is unchanged.

findings_remediated.finding: The mapped sources supported Critical Path Analysis generally but did not directly substantiate the total-float definition/calculation.
findings_remediated.remediation: Add a CC BY source explicitly defining project float/slack as latest start/finish minus earliest start/finish. Teaching content is unchanged.

findings_remediated.finding: The node correctly teaches validity, reliability, fairness, job relevance, bias and accessibility in selection, but its mapped promotion sources did not directly substantiate those concepts sufficiently.
findings_remediated.remediation: Add direct CC BY evidence for validity/reliability in employee selection and current OGL UK guidance for structured fair interviews and accessible/reasonably adjusted recruitment. Teaching content is unchanged.

source_additions.title: Capacity utilization under credit constraints: A firm-level study of Latin American manufacturing
source_additions.date_version: First published 2020-08-14; open-access article and licence/content checked 2026-09-28
source_additions.educational_role: Direct reusable support for capacity utilisation as actual/current output relative to maximum/potential output with required resources available, and for interpreting spare/unused capacity.
source_additions.restrictions: Use the article's CC BY 4.0 textual content only; retain Revision-authored Level 3 Business prose and do not import advanced econometric treatment as required learner content.

source_additions.issuer: A. Butrat and S. Supsomboon / Advances in Production Engineering & Management
source_additions.title: A Plant Simulation approach for optimal resource utilization: A case study in the tire manufacturing industry
source_additions.date_version: Volume 17 No. 2, 2022; DOI 10.14743/apem2022.2.434; CC BY 4.0 and content checked 2026-09-28
source_additions.educational_role: Direct reusable support for bottlenecks as capacity-constraining resources and their relationship to utilisation and production-volume limits.
source_additions.restrictions: Use the general bottleneck/capacity mechanism only; exclude specialised simulation detail and third-party referenced material from the reusable Level 3 teaching basis.

source_additions.issuer: Yu-Cheng Wang, Toly Chen and Yu-Cheng Lin / MDPI Healthcare
source_additions.title: A Collaborative and Ubiquitous System for Fabricating Dental Parts Using 3D Printing Technologies
source_additions.date_version: Published 2019-09-06; DOI 10.3390/healthcare7030103; CC BY 4.0 and content checked 2026-09-28
source_additions.educational_role: Direct reusable support for the project-management definition/calculation of float or slack as latest start/finish minus earliest start/finish and the meaning of delay without postponing project completion.
source_additions.restrictions: Use only the general project-float definition and relationship; the dental/3D-printing application and optimisation detail are not Level 3 Business teaching requirements.

source_additions.issuer: Kelechi Ekuma / Canadian Center of Science and Education
source_additions.title: The Importance of Predictive and Face Validity in Employee Selection and Ways of Maximizing Them: An Assessment of Three Selection Methods
source_additions.date_version: International Journal of Business and Management 7(22), 2012; DOI 10.5539/ijbm.v7n22p115; CC BY 4.0 and content checked 2026-09-28
source_additions.educational_role: Direct reusable support for validity, reliability and predictive relevance when evaluating employee-selection methods including interviews, work samples and assessment centres.
source_additions.restrictions: Use as evidence for general selection-quality concepts; do not treat one paper's recommendations as universal hiring law or replace current UK equality/accessibility guidance.

source_additions.issuer: UK Office for Equality and Opportunity
source_additions.title: Use fair and structured interview techniques
source_additions.educational_role: Current UK reusable support for job-relevant structured questions, standardised scoring, fairness, consistency and reducing bias in interviews.
source_additions.restrictions: Subject to GOV.UK page-specific exclusions and third-party rights; use for current UK hiring-process context rather than as a complete theory of selection validity.

source_additions.title: Recruitment and disabled people: Reasonable adjustments
source_additions.educational_role: Current UK reusable support for accessibility and reasonable adjustments in recruitment and selection processes.
source_additions.restrictions: Subject to GOV.UK page-specific exclusions and third-party rights; legal requirements are time-sensitive and exact-course learner wording must not be presented as legal advice.
